definition_en: to hand something to someone, to donate, or to yield
core_image: 双手把一件东西递到别人面前
scene: 请把盐递给我。Please give me the salt.
sceneCN: 这里 give 是「递给」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把盐递给我。

senses.title: To hand something over
senses.definition: to hand something to someone so they can have it
senses.definitionCN: 把某物递到别人手里让对方持有
senses.example: Please give me the salt.
senses.why: This is the central physical sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最核心的物理含义。

senses.title: To donate
senses.definition: to hand something over without asking for payment
senses.definitionCN: 把东西交出去而不索取报酬
senses.example: She gave her old books to the school.
senses.why: Giving without return is giving at its fullest.
senses.whyCN: 不求回报地给，是「给」最充分的形态。

senses.title: To yield
senses.definition: to stop resisting and accept what others want
senses.definitionCN: 停止抵抗，接受别人的要求
senses.example: He gave in after a long argument.
senses.exampleCN: 争论了很久之后他让步了。
senses.why: To give ground is to hand over your position.
senses.whyCN: 让出阵地，就是把自己的位置交出去。

intro.en: Give is an old Germanic verb with the same shape across many languages.
intro.cn: give 是一个古老的日耳曼动词，在多种语言中形态相近。

items.en: Giefan meant to give or to grant.
items.cn: giefan 意为给予或授予。

items.en: The form became given and kept both senses.
items.cn: 词形变为 given，保留了两个含义。

items.en: The verb extended to abstract gifts such as advice.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到建议等抽象的「给予」。

items.en: Phrases like give up and give in added new meanings.
items.cn: give up、give in 等短语增加了新的含义。

items.en: The past participle given became an adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 given 演变为形容词。

note.en: Give is compared with look-alike words and words for handing over.
note.cn: 把 give 与形近词以及表示交付的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Give is the open hand moving outward.
normalIntro.cn: give 是张开的手向外递出的动作。

normal.en: Please give me the salt.
She gave her old books to the school.
He gave in after a long argument.
normal.cn: 争论了很久之后他让步了。

normal.en: Can you give me a hand?
Do not give up so easily.

abstract.en: To give is to loosen the grip of the self.
abstract.cn: 给予，就是放松自我的抓握。

abstract.en: What is given freely returns in another form.
abstract.cn: 自由给出的东西，会以另一种形式回来。

abstract.en: A hand that gives is never truly empty.
abstract.cn: 给予的手，从不会真正空着。

examples.en: Please give me the salt.
She gave her old books to the school.
He gave in after a long argument.
examples.cn: 争论了很久之后他让步了。

dict_mnemonic.text: give 的过去式是 gave，过去分词是 given；give up 是「放弃」，give in 是「让步」，give away 是「赠送、泄露」，give rise to 是「引起」。

root: 来自古英语 giefan（给予），属日耳曼语族，核心义由「递交实物」扩展到「捐赠」与「让步」。

sensesIntro.en: Give means to hand something over, to donate it, or to yield a position.
sensesIntro.cn: give 意为把东西递出去、捐赠出去，或让出立场。

core.en: An open hand moving toward another.
core.cn: 一只张开的手伸向他人。

branches.en: Two hands meet over a salt cellar.
branches.cn: 两只手在盐罐上方相遇。

branches.en: A box of books is set at a school door.
branches.cn: 一箱书被放在学校门口。

branches.en: A debater lowers his hand and sits down.
branches.cn: 辩论者放下手，坐了下来。

branches.en: Handing over and giving away share one gesture.
branches.cn: 递交与赠予共享同一个手势。

branches.en: To give a thing and to give ground both mean letting go.
branches.cn: 给出东西与让出立场，都是放手。

intro.en: Give builds its forms by changing the stem vowel.
intro.cn: give 通过改变词干元音来构成各种形式。

latinIntro.en: Give has no Latin root; it comes from Old English giefan.
latinIntro.cn: give 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 giefan。

definition_zh: 高兴的；乐意的；令人高兴的
definition_en: pleased and happy, willing, or bringing joy
core_image: 一个人听到好消息，脸上一下子明亮起来
scene: 见到你我很高兴。I am glad to see you.
sceneCN: 这里 glad 是「高兴的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：见到你我很高兴。

senses.title: Pleased
senses.definition: feeling pleasure about something
senses.definitionCN: 因某事而感到愉快
senses.example: I am glad to see you.
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of personal pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示个人喜悦的日常含义。

senses.title: Willing
senses.definition: ready and willing to do something
senses.definitionCN: 愿意并且乐于做某事
senses.example: I am glad to help.
senses.why: A happy heart is a willing hand.
senses.whyCN: 心里高兴，手就愿意伸出去。

senses.title: Bringing joy
senses.definition: causing happiness
senses.definitionCN: 带来快乐的
senses.example: He brought glad news from home.
senses.why: The word can describe the news as well as the listener.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能形容听消息的人，也能形容消息本身。

intro.en: Glad first meant bright, and brightness became happiness.
intro.cn: glad 最初意为明亮，明亮后来变成了快乐。

items.en: Glæd meant bright, shining, or cheerful.
items.cn: glæd 意为明亮的、闪耀的或快活的。

items.en: The form became glad and kept the sense of joy.
items.cn: 词形变为 glad，保留了喜悦的含义。

items.en: It came to mean pleased about a particular thing.
items.cn: 它开始表示因某件具体的事而高兴。

items.en: The sense of willingness grew from happiness.
items.cn: 「乐意」的含义由快乐引申而来。

items.en: Glad tidings fixed the word in good news.
items.cn: glad tidings 把这个词固定用在好消息上。

note.en: Glad is compared with look-alike words and words for happiness.
note.cn: 把 glad 与形近词以及表示快乐的词作比较。

entries.definition: an open space in a forest

normalIntro.en: Glad is the light that switches on in the face.
normalIntro.cn: glad 是脸上忽然亮起的那盏灯。

normal.en: I am glad to see you.
I am glad to help.
He brought glad news from home.
She was glad about the result.
We are glad of your company.

abstract.en: Glad is a small sun rising behind the eyes.
abstract.cn: glad 是在眼睛后面升起的一轮小太阳。

abstract.en: A glad heart makes heavy work light.
abstract.cn: 心里高兴，重活也变轻。

abstract.en: What makes us glad tells us who we are.
abstract.cn: 让我们高兴的事，说明了我们是谁。

examples.en: I am glad to see you.
I am glad to help.
He brought glad news from home.

dict_mnemonic.text: glad 与 gladly（高兴地）、gladness（喜悦）、gladden（使高兴）同族；be glad to 表示「乐意」，glad tidings 是「喜讯」。

root: 来自古英语 glæd（明亮的、快活的），核心义由「光亮」转为「心里明亮、高兴」。

sensesIntro.en: Glad means pleased, willing, or bringing happiness.
sensesIntro.cn: glad 意为高兴的、乐意的，或带来快乐的。

core.en: A bright feeling inside.
core.cn: 内心明亮的感觉。

branches.en: A face lights up at a familiar voice.
branches.cn: 听到熟悉的声音，脸一下子亮了。

branches.en: A hand reaches out before being asked.
branches.cn: 还没被请求，手就伸了出去。

branches.en: A letter carries good news into a house.
branches.cn: 一封信把好消息带进屋里。

branches.en: Pleasure and willingness grow from one root.
branches.cn: 喜悦与乐意，同出一根。

branches.en: Glad news makes glad helpers.
branches.cn: 喜讯造就乐意的帮手。

intro.en: Glad forms adverbs, nouns, and verbs with -ly, -ness, and -en.
intro.cn: glad 与 -ly、-ness、-en 构成副词、名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: Glad has no Latin root; it comes from Old English glæd.
latinIntro.cn: glad 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 glæd。

items.example: I am glad to see you.
This is the gladdest day of my life.
items.exampleCN: 这是我一生中最高兴的一天。
那是个令人愉快的早晨。

definition_en: a quick look, to look quickly, or to read through briefly
core_image: 走路时目光迅速扫过街边的一扇窗
scene: 她朝窗外瞥了一眼。She glanced at the window.
sceneCN: 这里 glance 是「瞥一眼」（第 2 个义项）；句意：她朝窗外瞥了一眼。

senses.title: A quick look
senses.definition: a short look at something
senses.definitionCN: 朝某物匆匆看一眼
senses.example: She took a quick glance at the clock.
senses.why: The noun names the brief act itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接命名这个短暂的动作。

senses.title: To look quickly
senses.definition: to look at something for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 短暂地看某物一眼
senses.example: She glanced at the window.
senses.why: The verb turns the brief look into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把短暂的一看变成动作。

senses.title: To read through quickly
senses.definition: to read something quickly and not deeply
senses.definitionCN: 快速地、不深入地读某物
senses.example: He glanced through the report.
senses.exampleCN: 他草草浏览了那份报告。
senses.why: The eye that grazes a page reads only its surface.
senses.whyCN: 目光在纸面上轻轻掠过，只读到表层。

intro.en: Glance first meant to slide or graze, then a sliding look.
intro.cn: glance 最初意为滑动或擦过，后来指滑过的一眼。

items.en: Glacier meant to slide or slip.
items.cn: glacier 意为滑动或滑倒。

items.en: Glacen meant to move quickly and lightly.
items.cn: glacen 意为轻快地移动。

items.en: The word came to mean to strike and slide off.
items.cn: 这个词开始表示击中后擦过。

items.en: The eye's light touch became a glance.
items.cn: 目光的轻触变成了「一瞥」。

items.en: Glance through extended it to quick reading.
items.cn: glance through 把它扩展到快速阅读。

note.en: Glance is compared with look-alike words and words for looking.
note.cn: 把 glance 与形近词以及表示看的词作比较。

entries.definition: an open space in a forest
to look through a narrow opening
to direct the eyes at something

normalIntro.en: A glance is the eye touching something and moving on.
normalIntro.cn: 一瞥，是目光触到某物随即移开。

normal.en: She took a quick glance at the clock.
She glanced at the window.
He glanced through the report.
normal.cn: 他草草浏览了那份报告。

normal.en: At a glance, the two pictures look the same.
normal.cn: 乍一看，这两幅画是一样的。

normal.en: He cast a glance over his shoulder.

abstract.en: A glance is a look that refuses to stay.
abstract.cn: 一瞥，是不肯停留的目光。

abstract.en: The first glance often writes the first judgement.
abstract.cn: 第一眼，常常写下第一个判断。

abstract.en: Some truths are only seen in a glance.
abstract.cn: 有些真相，只在匆匆一瞥中显现。

examples.en: She took a quick glance at the clock.
She glanced at the window.
He glanced through the report.
examples.cn: 他草草浏览了那份报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: glance 与 glare（眩光）、glass（玻璃）形近，注意区分；at a glance 是「一眼就」，glance at 是「瞥一眼」，glance through 是「浏览」。

root: 来自古法语 glacier（滑动），经中古英语 glacen（轻快移动）发展为一瞥，核心意象是目光轻轻滑过。

sensesIntro.en: Glance means a quick look, the act of looking quickly, or a brief reading.
sensesIntro.cn: glance 指匆匆一看、快速看这个动作，或草草浏览。

core.en: The eye sliding across a surface.
core.cn: 目光在表面轻轻滑过。

branches.en: A clock face catches one second of attention.
branches.cn: 钟面只赢得一秒钟的注意。

branches.en: A passer-by turns her head toward a window.
branches.cn: 路人把头转向一扇窗。

branches.en: A thumb flips through pages.
branches.cn: 拇指翻过一页页纸。

branches.en: The noun and the verb are one brief motion.
branches.cn: 名词与动词是同一个短暂的动作。

branches.en: Looking at a page and reading it lightly are neighbours.
branches.cn: 看一页纸与轻轻读它，是邻居。

intro.en: Glance forms a verb paradigm and a few derived words.
intro.cn: glance 构成动词变化形式和少量派生词。

latinIntro.en: Glance has no Latin root; it comes from Old French glacier.
latinIntro.cn: glance 没有拉丁词根，它来自古法语 glacier。

items.example: She took a quick glance at the clock.
She looked glancingly at the letter.
items.exampleCN: 她匆匆看了一眼那封信。

items.example: He caught a glimpse of her.
Do not peek at the answers.

items.meaning: a look through a small opening

definition_en: a hard transparent material, a drinking container, or spectacles
core_image: 阳光穿过一只透明的玻璃杯，在桌上留下亮斑
scene: 请递给我一杯水。Please pass me a glass of water.
sceneCN: 这里 glass 是「玻璃杯」（第 2 个义项）；句意：请递给我一杯水。

senses.title: The material
senses.definition: a hard, transparent material made from sand
senses.definitionCN: 由沙子制成、坚硬透明的材料
senses.example: The window is made of glass.
senses.why: The material sense is the oldest and most general.
senses.whyCN: 材料义最古老，也最普遍。

senses.title: A drinking container
senses.definition: a container made of glass for drinking
senses.definitionCN: 用玻璃制成、用来喝水的容器
senses.example: Please pass me a glass of water.
senses.why: A thing made of glass took the name of the material.
senses.whyCN: 用玻璃做成的器物，继承了材料的名字。

senses.title: Spectacles
senses.definition: a pair of lenses worn to help you see
senses.definitionCN: 戴在眼上帮助视物的镜片
senses.example: He wears glasses for reading.
senses.why: Two lenses of glass became a pair of glasses.
senses.whyCN: 两片玻璃镜片，成了一副眼镜。

intro.en: Glass came from a Germanic word that may once have meant amber.
intro.cn: glass 来自一个日耳曼词，最初可能指琥珀。

items.en: Glæs meant glass and also amber.
items.cn: glæs 意为玻璃，也指琥珀。

items.en: The form became glas and named the material.
items.cn: 词形变为 glas，指称这种材料。

items.en: A drinking vessel took the same name.
items.cn: 饮水器皿也用了这个名字。

items.en: The plural glasses came to mean spectacles.
items.cn: 复数 glasses 开始表示眼镜。

items.en: The word entered compounds such as glasshouse.
items.cn: 这个词进入 glasshouse 等复合词。

note.en: Glass is compared with look-alike words and drinking vessels.
note.cn: 把 glass 与形近词以及饮水器皿作比较。

entries.definition: a sheet of glass in a window

normalIntro.en: Glass is sand that learned to let light through.
normalIntro.cn: 玻璃，是学会了让光通过的沙子。

normal.en: The window is made of glass.
Please pass me a glass of water.
He wears glasses for reading.
Be careful of the broken glass.
Rain ran down the glass pane.

abstract.en: Glass is a wall you can see through.
abstract.cn: 玻璃是一堵能看穿的墙。

abstract.en: A glass both holds water and shows the world.
abstract.cn: 玻璃杯既盛着水，也映着世界。

abstract.en: What is clear is also fragile.
abstract.cn: 清澈之物，也往往易碎。

examples.en: The window is made of glass.
Please pass me a glass of water.
He wears glasses for reading.

dict_mnemonic.text: glass 是玻璃，a glass of 是「一杯」，复数 glasses 常指眼镜；注意与 grass（草）、class（班级）区分首字母。

root: 来自古英语 glæs（玻璃、琥珀），属日耳曼语族，核心义由材料扩展到杯子和眼镜。

sensesIntro.en: Glass means the material, a drinking container made of it, or a pair of spectacles.
sensesIntro.cn: glass 指玻璃这种材料、玻璃杯，或一副眼镜。

core.en: Hard, clear matter that light passes through.
core.cn: 光可以穿过的坚硬透明物质。

branches.en: A window shines in the morning sun.
branches.cn: 一扇窗在晨光中发亮。

branches.en: Water is poured into a clear cup.
branches.cn: 水被倒进一只透明的杯子。

branches.en: Two round lenses rest on a nose.
branches.cn: 两片圆形镜片架在鼻梁上。

branches.en: The material and the vessel share one word.
branches.cn: 材料与器皿共用一个词。

branches.en: A glass to drink from and glasses to see through.
branches.cn: 一只用来喝的玻璃杯，一副用来看的眼镜。

intro.en: Glass builds adjectives, measures, and compounds.
intro.cn: glass 构成形容词、量词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Glass has no Latin root; it comes from Old English glæs.
latinIntro.cn: glass 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 glæs。

items.example: The window is made of glass.
The lake was glassy and still.
She drank a glassful of milk.
The boat is made of fiberglass.
items.exampleCN: 这条船是玻璃纤维做的。

items.example: The church has stained glass windows.

definition_en: a very brief look, to see briefly, or a short understanding
core_image: 人群中一闪而过的熟悉面孔
scene: 他透过人群瞥见了她。He caught a glimpse of her through the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 glimpse 是「一瞥」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他透过人群瞥见了她。

senses.title: A very brief look
senses.definition: a quick and incomplete view of something
senses.definitionCN: 短暂而不完整地看到某物
senses.example: He caught a glimpse of her through the crowd.
senses.why: The noun names a view too short to be complete.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名一个短到来不及完整的视野。

senses.title: To see briefly
senses.definition: to see something for only a moment
senses.definitionCN: 只在刹那间看到某物
senses.example: She glimpsed a fox at the edge of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 她瞥见树林边有一只狐狸。
senses.why: The verb turns the brief sight into an act.
senses.whyCN: 动词把短暂看见变成动作。

senses.title: A short understanding
senses.definition: a brief experience that shows you something
senses.definitionCN: 让人窥见某事的短暂体验
senses.example: The visit gave us a glimpse of village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这次访问让我们窥见了乡村生活。
senses.why: Seeing a little of a thing is also understanding a little.
senses.whyCN: 看到事物的一小部分，也就是理解了一小部分。

intro.en: Glimpse began as a faint shining, then a flash of sight.
intro.cn: glimpse 最初指微弱的光，后来指目光的一闪。

items.en: Glim meant a brightness or a glow.
items.cn: glim 意为光亮或微光。

items.en: Glimsen meant to shine faintly.
items.cn: glimsen 意为微微发亮。

items.en: The word came to mean a brief flash of sight.
items.cn: 这个词开始表示视觉上的一闪。

items.en: The verb glimpsed added the act of seeing.
items.cn: 动词 glimpsed 增加了「看见」的动作。

items.en: A glimpse of truth extended it to understanding.
items.cn: a glimpse of truth 把它扩展到理解层面。

note.en: Glimpse is compared with look-alike words and words for brief looking.
note.cn: 把 glimpse 与形近词以及表示短暂观看的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A glimpse is a window opened for a second and shut.
normalIntro.cn: glimpse 是一扇开了一秒就关上的窗。

normal.en: He caught a glimpse of her through the crowd.
She glimpsed a fox at the edge of the wood.
normal.cn: 她瞥见树林边有一只狐狸。

normal.en: The visit gave us a glimpse of village life.
normal.cn: 这次访问让我们窥见了乡村生活。

normal.en: A glimpse of the sea appeared between the hills.
He glimpsed at the letter and put it down.
normal.cn: 他朝信瞥了一眼就放下了。

abstract.en: A glimpse is enough to change what we believe.
abstract.cn: 一瞥，足以改变我们所相信的东西。

abstract.en: What we glimpse, we remember longer than what we study.
abstract.cn: 瞥见的东西，比攻读的东西记得更久。

abstract.en: Every great discovery begins with a glimpse.
abstract.cn: 每一项伟大发现，都始于一眼。

examples.en: He caught a glimpse of her through the crowd.
She glimpsed a fox at the edge of the wood.
examples.cn: 她瞥见树林边有一只狐狸。

examples.en: The visit gave us a glimpse of village life.
examples.cn: 这次访问让我们窥见了乡村生活。

examples.en: Do not forget your gloves before going out.

definition_en: to give off a steady light, a soft radiance, or a warm feeling
core_image: 壁炉里的余烬仍然发着暗红的光
scene: 炉火在壁炉里发出红光。The fire glowed in the hearth.
sceneCN: 这里 glow 是「发光」（第 1 个义项）；句意：炉火在壁炉里发出红光。

senses.title: To give off light
senses.definition: to send out a steady light and heat without flames
senses.definitionCN: 没有火焰却持续发出光和热
senses.example: The fire glowed in the hearth.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火在壁炉里发出红光。
senses.why: This is the physical sense at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最核心的物理含义。

senses.title: A soft radiance
senses.definition: a steady, soft light
senses.definitionCN: 稳定而柔和的光
senses.example: The glow of the lamp filled the room.
senses.why: The noun names the light that the verb produces.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名动词所产生的光。

senses.title: A warm feeling
senses.definition: a feeling of warmth, health, or happiness that shows
senses.definitionCN: 流露在外的温暖、健康或幸福之感
senses.example: Her face had a healthy glow.
senses.exampleCN: 她脸上泛着健康的光泽。
senses.why: Light inside a person shows on the face.
senses.whyCN: 人内在的光，会显在脸上。

intro.en: Glow is an old Germanic verb for burning without flame.
intro.cn: glow 是一个古老的日耳曼动词，指无焰地燃烧。

items.en: Glowan meant to glow or to shine with heat.
items.cn: glowan 意为发光或因热而发亮。

items.en: The form became glowen.
items.cn: 词形变为 glowen。

items.en: The verb named the light of embers and lamps.
items.cn: 这个动词指余烬与灯的光。

items.en: The noun named the light itself.
items.cn: 名词指光本身。

items.en: The word extended to the warmth of health and feeling.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到健康与情感的温度。

note.en: Glow is compared with look-alike words and words for shining.
note.cn: 把 glow 与形近词以及表示发光的词作比较。

entries.definition: to send out light or heat

normalIntro.en: Glow is light that stays and breathes.
normalIntro.cn: glow 是留下来、会呼吸的光。

normal.en: The fire glowed in the hearth.
normal.cn: 炉火在壁炉里发出红光。

normal.en: The glow of the lamp filled the room.
Her face had a healthy glow.
normal.cn: 她脸上泛着健康的光泽。

normal.en: The stars glowed above the lake.
He glowed with pride at the news.
normal.cn: 听到这个消息，他满面自豪。

abstract.en: Glow is what fire leaves when it chooses to stay.
abstract.cn: glow 是火选择留下时留下的东西。

abstract.en: A quiet glow outlasts a bright flame.
abstract.cn: 安静的光，比明亮的火焰更持久。

abstract.en: People glow when they are fully themselves.
abstract.cn: 人做回自己时，会发光。

examples.en: The fire glowed in the hearth.

examples.en: The glow of the lamp filled the room.
Her face had a healthy glow.
examples.cn: 她脸上泛着健康的光泽。

dict_mnemonic.text: glow 与 slow（慢）、grow（生长）、flow（流动）押韵，注意区分；glowing 是「发光的、热情的」，afterglow 是「余晖」，glow with pride 表示「满面自豪」。

root: 来自古英语 glowan（发光、发热），属日耳曼语族，核心义由无焰燃烧的光扩展到面色与情感的光彩。

sensesIntro.en: Glow means to give off steady light, the light itself, or a warm look of feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: glow 意为持续发光、所发之光，或情感流露的暖色。

core.en: Heat that shines without a flame.
core.cn: 没有火焰却在发亮的热。

branches.en: Embers breathe red in a fireplace.
branches.cn: 余烬在壁炉里透出红色。

branches.en: A lamp fills a room with soft light.
branches.cn: 一盏灯用柔光充满房间。

branches.en: A face shines after good news.
branches.cn: 听到好消息，脸上一亮。

branches.en: The act and the light are one warmth.
branches.cn: 发光的动作与光，是同一份温暖。

branches.en: Outer light is a picture of inner warmth.
branches.cn: 外在的光，是内在温暖的写照。

intro.en: Glow forms verbs, adjectives, and compounds.
intro.cn: glow 构成动词、形容词和复合词。

definition_en: a sticky substance for joining things, to stick things together, or to hold attention
core_image: 一张纸被胶水牢牢粘在另一张纸上
scene: 他用胶水把纸粘在一起。He used glue to stick the papers together.
sceneCN: 这里 glue 是「胶水」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用胶水把纸粘在一起。

senses.title: A sticky substance
senses.definition: a substance used to stick things together
senses.definitionCN: 用来把东西粘在一起的材料
senses.example: He used glue to stick the papers together.
senses.exampleCN: 他用胶水把纸粘在一起。
senses.why: This is the concrete sense of the material.
senses.whyCN: 这是这种材料的具体含义。

senses.title: To stick together
senses.definition: to join things with a sticky substance
senses.definitionCN: 用黏性物质把东西连接起来
senses.example: She glued the pieces of the vase.
senses.exampleCN: 她把花瓶的碎片粘了起来。
senses.why: The material became a verb for using it.
senses.whyCN: 材料名转为使用它的动词。

senses.title: To hold attention
senses.definition: to keep someone's eyes or attention fixed
senses.definitionCN: 让某人的目光或注意力牢牢固定住
senses.example: The child was glued to the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子目不转睛地盯着屏幕。
senses.why: Attention stuck to a thing is like paper stuck to paper.
senses.whyCN: 注意力粘在事物上，就像纸粘在纸上。

intro.en: Glue goes back to a Latin word for a sticky animal substance.
intro.cn: glue 可追溯到拉丁语中表示黏性动物物质的一个词。

items.en: Gluten meant glue, made from animal hides.
items.cn: gluten 意为胶，由动物皮制成。

items.en: Glu named a sticky substance.
items.cn: glu 指黏性物质。

items.en: Glu entered English as a material word.
items.cn: glu 作为材料词进入英语。

items.en: The verb glue meant to fix with glue.
items.cn: 动词 glue 意为用胶固定。

note.en: Glue is compared with look-alike words and sticky substances.

normalIntro.en: Glue is the word for making two things one.

abstract.en: What is glued can still come apart.

examples.en: He used glue to stick the papers together.

sensesIntro.en: Glue means a sticky material, the act of sticking things, or holding attention fixed.

core.en: A substance that makes two surfaces one.

branches.en: A bottle of glue stands open on a desk.
branches.cn: 一瓶胶水开着盖放在桌上。

branches.en: Eyes stay fixed on a bright screen.

branches.en: Paper and attention are both held by glue.
branches.cn: 纸与注意力，都能被「胶」粘住。

intro.en: Glue forms verbs, an adjective, and a compound.
intro.cn: glue 构成动词、形容词和一个复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is gluten, meaning glue.

definition_en: to move to another place, to become, or to turn out
core_image: 一条小路从脚下伸向远方的山坡
scene: 我们明天去海边吧。Let us go to the beach tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 go 是「去」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们明天去海边吧。

senses.title: To move to a place
senses.definition: to move or travel from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方移动到另一个地方
senses.example: Let us go to the beach tomorrow.
senses.why: This is the central sense of movement.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示移动的核心含义。

senses.title: To become
senses.definition: to change into a particular state
senses.definitionCN: 变成某种特定的状态
senses.example: The milk went bad in the heat.
senses.why: To go into a state is to arrive at it.
senses.whyCN: 进入一种状态，就是抵达那种状态。

senses.title: To turn out
senses.definition: to happen or develop in a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式发生或发展
senses.example: The meeting went well.
senses.why: Events go along a path just as people do.
senses.whyCN: 事件和人一样，也沿着一条路前行。

intro.en: Go is one of the oldest verbs in English, with an irregular past.
intro.cn: go 是英语中最古老的动词之一，过去式不规则。

items.en: Gan meant to go or to walk.
items.cn: gan 意为去或走。

items.en: The form became gon and then go.
items.cn: 词形先变为 gon，再变为 go。

items.en: The past went was borrowed from the verb wend.
items.cn: 过去式 went 借自动词 wend。

items.en: Go came to mean to become, as in go bad.
items.cn: go 开始表示「变得」，如 go bad。

items.en: Phrasal verbs like go on and go out multiplied its uses.
items.cn: go on、go out 等短语动词大大扩展了它的用法。

items.en: Going became a noun for speed and progress.
items.cn: going 成为表示速度与进展的名词。

note.en: Go is compared with look-alike words and verbs of movement.
note.cn: 把 go 与形近词以及表示移动的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to go away from a place

normalIntro.en: Go is the shortest word for leaving here for there.
normalIntro.cn: go 是「从这里到那里」最短的词。

normal.en: Let us go to the beach tomorrow.
The milk went bad in the heat.
The meeting went well.
She goes to school by bus.
Do not let the fire go out.

abstract.en: To go is to trust that somewhere else is worth reaching.
abstract.cn: 出发，就是相信别处值得抵达。

abstract.en: Time goes whether or not we move.
abstract.cn: 无论我们是否移动，时间都在走。

abstract.en: What goes around comes around.
abstract.cn: 走了一圈的东西，终会回来。

examples.en: Let us go to the beach tomorrow.
The milk went bad in the heat.
The meeting went well.

sensesIntro.en: Go means to move to a place, to become a state, or to develop in some way.

core.en: Movement away from here toward there.
core.cn: 从这里向那里的移动。

branches.en: A path leads from the door to the sea.
branches.cn: 一条小路从门口通向大海。

branches.en: Milk sours on a warm table.
branches.cn: 牛奶在温暖的桌上变酸。

branches.en: A meeting ends with nods and smiles.
branches.cn: 会议在点头与微笑中结束。

branches.en: Moving into a state is arriving somewhere new.
branches.cn: 进入一种状态，就是抵达一个新地方。

branches.en: Things and people both go along a road.
branches.cn: 事物与人，都沿着一条路走。

intro.en: Go has irregular forms and builds compounds with -ing and out-.
intro.cn: go 有规则外的变化形式，并与 -ing、out- 构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Go has no Latin root; it comes from Old English gan.
latinIntro.cn: go 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 gan。

She is a regular cinema goer.

definition_en: an aim you work toward, the frame where players score, or a point scored

scene: 他的目标是今年读五十本书。His goal is to read fifty books this year.
sceneCN: 这里 goal 是「目标」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的目标是今年读五十本书。

senses.title: An aim
senses.definition: something you hope to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 你希望达成的事情
senses.example: His goal is to read fifty books this year.
senses.exampleCN: 他的目标是今年读五十本书。
senses.why: This is the central modern sense of purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最核心的「目的」含义。

senses.title: The scoring frame
senses.definition: the frame into which players try to send the ball
senses.definitionCN: 球员努力把球送进去的框架
senses.example: The ball hit the goal and bounced out.
senses.exampleCN: 球击中球门后弹了出来。
senses.why: The end point of play became the word for the frame.
senses.whyCN: 比赛的终点，成了这个框架的名字。

senses.title: A point scored
senses.definition: a point won by sending the ball into the goal
senses.definitionCN: 把球送入球门而赢得的一分
senses.example: He scored two goals in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛中进了两个球。
senses.why: The frame and the score share one word.

dict_mnemonic.text: golf 是高尔夫球运动，play golf 是「打高尔夫球」；golf course 是「球场」，golf club 是「球杆、俱乐部」，golfer 是「球手」；注意与 gold（黄金）区分。

root: 可能来自荷兰语 colf 或斯堪的纳维亚语 kolbe（球杆），核心义由球杆转为这项运动本身。

sensesIntro.en: Golf means the game, the ball used in it, or the act of playing it.
sensesIntro.cn: golf 指这项运动、所用的球，或打这项运动。

core.en: A club, a ball, and a distant hole.
core.cn: 一根球杆、一颗球和一个远处的洞。

branches.en: A player walks a green course.
branches.cn: 球手走在绿色球道上。

branches.en: A white ball rests on the grass.
branches.cn: 一颗白球停在草地上。

branches.en: A swing sends the ball into the sky.
branches.cn: 一挥杆，球飞向天空。

branches.en: The game and its ball share one name.
branches.cn: 运动与球共用一个名字。

branches.en: The ball waits to be played.
branches.cn: 球等着被打出去。

intro.en: Golf forms a verb paradigm and a few role words.
intro.cn: golf 构成动词变化形式和几个表示角色的词。

latinIntro.en: Golf has no Latin root; it comes from Dutch or Scandinavian.
latinIntro.cn: golf 没有拉丁词根，它来自荷兰语或斯堪的纳维亚语。

items.exampleCN: 他们每周末都打高尔夫球。
她是个热衷高尔夫球的人。

items.example: The golfers waited for the rain to stop.

items.exampleCN: 打高尔夫是他唯一的爱好。
他们打了一上午高尔夫球。

items.meaning: a light stroke on the green

items.example: The links are famous for wind.
items.exampleCN: 这处海滨球场以风大闻名。

definition_zh: 好的；擅长的；令人愉快的
definition_en: of high quality, skilled at something, or pleasant
core_image: 一只刚烤好的面包放在木桌上，香气扑鼻
scene: 这是一本好书。This is a good book.
sceneCN: 这里 good 是「好的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这是一本好书。

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: of a high standard or quality
senses.definitionCN: 标准或品质很高的
senses.example: This is a good book.
senses.why: This is the broad sense of approval.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的赞许含义。

senses.title: Skilled
senses.definition: able to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 能把某事做得很好的
senses.example: She is good at chess.
senses.why: A person of good ability is good at a task.
senses.whyCN: 能力强的人，就是「擅长」某项任务。

senses.title: Pleasant
senses.definition: enjoyable and pleasing
senses.definitionCN: 令人享受和愉悦的
senses.example: We had a good time at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在聚会上玩得很开心。
senses.why: What is good for us is often pleasant to us.
senses.whyCN: 对我们有益的东西，往往也令我们愉快。

intro.en: Good is an old Germanic word that once meant fitting or suitable.
intro.cn: good 是一个古老的日耳曼词，最初意为合适、恰当。

items.en: God meant good, fit, or suitable.
items.cn: god 意为好的、合适的、恰当的。

items.en: The form became good and widened in meaning.
items.cn: 词形变为 good，含义变宽。

items.en: The comparative became better from another root.
items.cn: 比较级 better 来自另一个词根。

items.en: Good at extended it to skill.
items.cn: good at 把它扩展到「擅长」。

items.en: Good for extended it to benefit.
items.cn: good for 把它扩展到「有益」。

items.en: A good deal fixed it as a phrase of quantity.
items.cn: a good deal 把它固定为数量短语。

note.en: Good is compared with look-alike words and words of praise.
note.cn: 把 good 与形近词以及表示赞许的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Good is the general word for things that deserve a yes.
normalIntro.cn: good 是对值得说「是」的事物的一般说法。

normal.en: This is a good book.
She is good at chess.
We had a good time at the party.
normal.cn: 我们在聚会上玩得很开心。

normal.en: Fresh air is good for you.
Good morning, everyone.

abstract.en: Good is a small word with a wide door.
abstract.cn: good 是一个词形小、门却很宽的字。

abstract.en: To be good at something is to give it attention.
abstract.cn: 擅长某事，就是把注意力给了它。

abstract.en: What is good for one may not be good for all.
abstract.cn: 对一人好的，未必对所有人都好。

examples.en: This is a good book.
She is good at chess.
We had a good time at the party.
examples.cn: 我们在聚会上玩得很开心。

dict_mnemonic.text: good 的比较级是 better，最高级是 best；be good at 是「擅长」，be good for 是「对……有益」，a good deal 是「大量」；注意与 god（神）区分。

root: 来自古英语 god（好的、合适的），属日耳曼语族，比较级 better、最高级 best 来自另一词根，核心义为「符合标准的」。

sensesIntro.en: Good means of high quality, skilled at something, or pleasant.
sensesIntro.cn: good 意为品质优良、擅长某事，或令人愉快。

core.en: Something that meets the standard we hold.
core.cn: 符合我们所持标准的事物。

branches.en: A warm loaf waits on a wooden table.
branches.cn: 一只热面包放在木桌上。

branches.en: A player moves a piece with confidence.
branches.cn: 棋手自信地移动棋子。

branches.en: Friends laugh around a table.
branches.cn: 朋友们围桌欢笑。

branches.en: A good thing and a good hand both meet a standard.
branches.cn: 好东西与好手，都符合某种标准。

branches.en: Skill and enjoyment often grow together.
branches.cn: 技艺与享受，常常一起生长。

intro.en: Good has irregular comparison and a family of derived nouns.
intro.cn: good 有不规则比较级，并构成一族派生名词。

latinIntro.en: Good has no Latin root; it comes from Old English god.
latinIntro.cn: good 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 god。

items.example: She is the best in the class.
The children got goodies at the party.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们在聚会上得到了好东西。

items.example: The gift was a sign of goodwill.
items.exampleCN: 这份礼物是善意的表示。

definition_en: the quality of being kind and good, moral virtue, or an exclamation of surprise
core_image: 有人默默把伞递给雨中的陌生人，没有留下名字
scene: 她待人的善良人人皆知。Her goodness to others is well known.
sceneCN: 这里 goodness 是「善良」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她待人的善良人人皆知。

senses.title: Kindness
senses.definition: the quality of being kind to others
senses.definitionCN: 待人友善的品质
senses.example: Her goodness to others is well known.
senses.exampleCN: 她待人的善良人人皆知。
senses.why: This is the central moral sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最核心的道德含义。

senses.title: Moral virtue
senses.definition: excellence of character
senses.definitionCN: 品性上的优良
senses.example: The story praises the goodness of ordinary people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事赞美普通人的美德。
senses.why: Goodness names the quality behind good acts.
senses.whyCN: goodness 命名好行为背后的品质。

senses.title: An exclamation
senses.definition: a mild exclamation of surprise
senses.definitionCN: 表示惊讶的温和感叹
senses.example: Goodness, is it that late?
senses.why: People call on goodness as they call on heaven.
senses.whyCN: 人们呼唤「善良」，如同呼唤上天。

intro.en: Goodness is good plus the old noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: goodness 由 good 加古老的名词后缀 -ness 构成。

items.en: Godnes meant goodness or virtue.
items.cn: godnes 意为善良或美德。

items.en: The form became goodnesse and named a virtue.
items.cn: 词形变为 goodnesse，指一种美德。

items.en: It named the kindly quality of a person.
items.cn: 它指人善良的品质。

items.en: It also became a mild exclamation.
items.cn: 它也成为温和的感叹词。

items.en: Phrases like thank goodness fixed the exclamation.
items.cn: thank goodness 等短语固定了这一感叹用法。

note.en: Goodness is compared with look-alike words and words for virtue.
note.cn: 把 goodness 与形近词以及表示美德的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Goodness is good made into a substance you can see in a person.
normalIntro.cn: goodness 是把 good 变成在人身上看得见的品质。

normal.en: Her goodness to others is well known.
normal.cn: 她待人的善良人人皆知。

normal.en: The story praises the goodness of ordinary people.
normal.cn: 这个故事赞美普通人的美德。

normal.en: Goodness, is it that late?
Thank goodness you are safe.
He believed in the goodness of human nature.

abstract.en: Goodness is kindness that does not need an audience.
abstract.cn: 善良，是不需要观众的善意。

abstract.en: The goodness of a person shows in small things.
abstract.cn: 一个人的善良，显在小事上。

abstract.en: Goodness given away is never lost.
abstract.cn: 给出去的善良，从不丢失。

examples.en: Her goodness to others is well known.
examples.cn: 她待人的善良人人皆知。

examples.en: The story praises the goodness of ordinary people.
examples.cn: 这个故事赞美普通人的美德。

examples.en: Goodness, is it that late?

dict_mnemonic.text: goodness 由 good 加 -ness 构成；thank goodness 是「谢天谢地」，for goodness' sake 是「看在老天份上」，goodness knows 是「天知道」；注意与 goods（商品）区分。

root: 来自古英语 godnes（善良、美德），由 good 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，核心义为善良品性，后引申为感叹词。

sensesIntro.en: Goodness means kindness, moral virtue, or a mild exclamation of surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: goodness 指善良、美德，或温和的惊讶感叹。

core.en: A kind heart made visible in action.
core.cn: 在行动中显形的善心。

branches.en: A stranger holds an umbrella over another.
branches.cn: 陌生人为别人撑起伞。

branches.en: A story praises quiet decency.
branches.cn: 一个故事赞美安静的正直。

branches.en: A hand rises to the mouth in surprise.
branches.cn: 一只手惊讶地掩住嘴。

branches.en: Kind acts grow from a virtuous character.
branches.cn: 善行生长于美德的品格。

branches.en: People call on goodness when words fail.
branches.cn: 无言以对时，人们呼唤「善良」。

intro.en: Goodness joins good with the noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: goodness 由 good 加名词后缀 -ness 构成。

latinIntro.en: Goodness is Germanic; Latin uses bonitas for the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: goodness 属日耳曼语；拉丁语用 bonitas 表达同一概念。

items.example: Her goodness to others is well known.
items.exampleCN: 她待人的善良人人皆知。

items.example: The children got goodies at the party.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们在聚会上得到了好东西。

items.example: The gift was a sign of goodwill.
items.exampleCN: 这份礼物是善意的表示。
